How to read a Delaware eviction notice

What the dates on an eviction notice mean, and how long a tenant actually has to respond at each stage.

How do I apply for SNAP benefits?

Apply online through Delaware ASSIST, by mail, or in person at a State Service Center.

What is the eviction notice period in Delaware?

5 days for nonpayment of rent, 7 days for lease violations, 60 days for no-cause termination.

Where can I get free legal help in Wilmington?

Delaware Volunteer Legal Services and Community Legal Aid Society both offer free civil legal help.

Delaware raises income threshold for Emergency Assistance eligibility

Delaware Health and Social Services

Effective July 1, Delaware DHSS raised the income threshold for Emergency Assistance — which covers rent, utilities, and emergency shelter — from 100% to 125% of the Federal Poverty Level.

2026-06-02

NEWS
West End Neighborhood House expands Life Lines to age 25

West End Neighborhood House

West End Neighborhood House has raised the age cap for its Life Lines youth housing program from 23 to 25, effective immediately. The program serves foster care and unaccompanied youth, including LGBTQ+ youth.

2026-05-30

What is the eviction notice period in Delaware?

First Step

What can I do if my landlord won't return my security deposit?

Delaware Volunteer Legal Services

Delaware law gives landlords 20 days to return a deposit or provide an itemized list of deductions.

2026-06-15

EXPERT
How much notice does my landlord have to give before eviction?

Delaware Volunteer Legal Services

Notice periods depend on the reason for eviction — from 5 days for nonpayment up to 60 days for no-cause termination of a year-to-year lease.

Delaware raises income threshold for Emergency Assistance eligibility

Effective July 1, Delaware DHSS raised the income threshold for Emergency Assistance — which covers rent, utilities, and emergency shelter — from 100% to 125% of the Federal Poverty Level.

Delaware Medicaid expansion covers dental for adults starting October 1

Delaware will begin covering comprehensive dental care for adult Medicaid enrollees on October 1, 2026 — a first for the state. This affects an estimated 70,000 Delaware adults currently on Medicaid.
